steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Each customer's aggregated usage reaches the metric store by business, customer and dimension. Each business keeps a billing catalogue in the billing bucket with plans, dimensions, allowances, overage rules, invoice settings and customer assignments. The invoicing collector already reads both. Charge only permitted usage beyond a finite exhausted allowance; an unlimited or unexhausted allowance, or a plan that forbids overage, charges nothing. Give a dimension a line whenever the customer owes something on it, and give a dimension the plan prices at zero a line unless the invoice settings hide free dimensions. A dimension's line reports the quantity the customer owes for, even where the plan prices it at zero. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

Don't break this.

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure

```

steps.message:
Lint is clean and the only type errors are pre-existing ones in the spec file (not in my modified entity code).

**Summary of the fix** (`src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts`):

1. Added `Offering.owedQuantity({ total, dimension })` — computes what a customer actually owes for on a non-tiered dimension:
   - no allowance (`usageEntitlement` null/undefined) → the whole usage total,
   - `'inf'` allowance → nothing,
   - finite allowance with `overageAllowed !== 'true'` → nothing (plan forbids overage),
   - finite allowance with overage permitted → only the usage beyond the allowance (0 if unexhausted).
2. Added `Offering.shouldAddDimensionLineItem({ owedQuantity, unitCost, settings })` — a dimension gets a line when the customer owes something on it; a dimension the plan prices at zero also gets a line unless `settings.freeDimensionOnInvoice === 'hide'`.
3. Wired both into `getLineItemsForUsage`: dimension totals are now reduced to the owed quantity (so the line reports the quantity owed for, even for zero-priced dimensions), and lines that qualify for neither rule are skipped (with a log line).

Verified against the local AWS emulator via the invoicing collector: Ridge (hides free dims) now bills API calls 100 @0.01 and 2 overage seats @10 only — free alerts hidden, no-overage reports, and `inf` storage dropped; Ridge Metered bills only jobs (unexhausted minutes, `inf` scans, and overage-forbidden tasks dropped); Vale (shows free dims) keeps messages, the zero-priced hours line with quantity 10, and 5 overage units.
